_comment: Lane definitions for arch-advisor. Override by copying this file to .arch-advisor/lanes.json in a project, to ~/.claude/arch-advisor/lanes.json for all projects, or by pointing $ARCH_ADVISOR_CONFIG at it. Each lane maps 1:1 to a shipped agent file: you can change a lane's model, effort rungs and timeout here without touching an agent, but adding a genuinely new lane also needs a new agents/*.md file, because Claude Code discovers agents statically at startup.
_efforts_note: Rungs below were verified empirically against the Codex CLI on 2026-09-05, not copied from docs. Both models reject 'minimal'. The API additionally accepts 'none' on gpt-5.6-luna (but not on gpt-6-astra); it is omitted here because an implementation lane should never run without reasoning. 'ultra' is not an API reasoning.effort value at all -- it is a Codex CLI construct that adds internal task delegation -- and it is accepted on both models, contrary to upstream's claim that it is Sol-only. It is verified working but DELIBERATELY NOT DECLARED here: it burns tokens fast enough that it should be an explicit, deliberate opt-in. Add the ultra string to a lane's efforts array to enable it; until then lane.sh refuses it like any other undeclared rung.

routine.route_when: The spec fully determines the outcome: mechanical edits, renames, wiring, boilerplate, tests that mirror an existing pattern, ordinary features with a design decision or two.

complex.route_when: Judgment the spec cannot capture decides the outcome: subtle concurrency, non-trivial algorithms, security-sensitive paths, gnarly debugging, wide-blast-radius refactors, or the routine lane already failed on a corrected spec. Also the second runner when racing two lanes on one spec.
